Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv:2405.21075.
creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun (Nanjing University, State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Intelligence, XMU, HKU, PKU, CUHK, ECNU, CASIA)
description: Video-MME is the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. It comprises 900 videos across 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, annotated with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice QA pairs (3 per video), covering short (11s), medium, and long (up to 1 hour) videos, and incorporating subtitles and audio tracks for comprehensive multimodal evaluation.
name: Video-MME
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 QA pairs per video (each with 4 candidate options)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning. Additional contributors acknowledged by name: Yu Bai, Fangyuan Liu, Yigeng Jiang, and Zezhong Wu.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement. The distribution of answer options (A/B/C/D) follows a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then iteratively created three relevant multiple-choice questions, each with four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. Questions cover 12 distinct task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair was designed to be closely tied to video content. A quality review process had each QA pair examined by a different annotator to verify: (i) language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options and the correct answer is appropriate. Additionally, text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content; questions where Gemini 1.5 Pro answered correctly were returned to the original annotator for revision.
rai:dataCollection: Videos were manually collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. For each category, videos were collected with varying duration lengths: short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes). Corresponding meta-information including subtitles (if provided) and audios were also obtained. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, 744 with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos sourced from YouTube spanning 6 visual domains and 30 fine-grained categories, along with their associated subtitles (if provided by the platform) and audio tracks.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reveals that all current MLLMs show a decline in performance as video duration increases, suggesting limitations in processing longer video sequences. Open-source models are limited by fixed numbers of input frames (e.g., 8 frames), resulting in excessively sparse information density for long videos. The benchmark focuses on multiple-choice QA format, which may not capture all aspects of video understanding.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were categorized into short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes) duration groups. Subtitles were obtained from YouTube if provided. For evaluation, subtitles corresponding to timestamps of sampled video frames are selected (e.g., if 10 frames are sampled, the 10 subtitles corresponding to those timestamps are used).
rai:dataSocialImpact: Video-MME is designed to advance research in multimodal understanding and push the development of MLLMs toward artificial general intelligence. The benchmark highlights the need for improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development. It provides a universal benchmark applicable to both image and video MLLMs.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating and benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) on video understanding tasks, including assessment of temporal understanding, multimodal input processing (video frames, subtitles, audio), and performance across varying video durations and domains. Applicable to both image-based and video-based MLLMs.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used during quality review to filter out QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions (without video content). Questions where Gemini 1.5 Pro answered correctly in text-only mode were returned to annotators for revision.
